html:
A huge group portrait painted by Rembrandt in 1642, showing a company of Amsterdam's civic militia led by Captain Frans Banninck Cocq. It hangs in the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam.

Militia groups often paid to be painted in neat rows. Rembrandt instead showed them in motion, as the captain gives the order to march. Men load muskets, a drummer beats, a dog barks, and a small girl in gold light carries a chicken, the company's emblem. The light picks out the captain and his lieutenant and leaves others in shadow.

It is a peak of the Dutch Golden Age, when the Dutch Republic was rich from trade and its citizens bought art. The name The Night Watch came later, because dark varnish had made the daytime scene look like night. In 1715 it was cut down on all sides to fit a wall in the town hall. It has been attacked several times and restored, and is now one of the most famous paintings in the world.
